messages:
inc-bot: ALERT: GeoDNS healthcheck failures detected across eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Affected records: api.redwood.example.com. High error rate (502/504) observed by edge probes. Page: selina (oncall) :rotating_light:

selina: ack. I'm on it, grabbing context. Starting an incident page: https://incident.redwood.internal/INC-20260315-01 :rotating_light:

noah: I'm seeing asymmetric DNS answers from Route53 vs Cloudflare in EU. Route53 healthchecks show 0.2% fail but edge resolvers returning stale A records for eu nodes.

selina: customer impact? any 5xx reported in metrics?

jamie: Metrics: spike in 502 and increased latency for EU customers, about 8% of requests failing from EU resolvers. Logs show backend healthy. Suspect DNS caching/resolver divergence.

noah: quick dig from our labs:
```
dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com A
# => 52.18.10.200

dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com A
# => 3.123.45.67
```
Different answers. Cloudflare edge returns 3.123.45.67 (healthy), Route53 returns 52.18.10.200 (stale/old) - Route53 TTL for that record is 300s but we pushed a change yesterday.

selina: can we force Route53 to publish a fresh zone change? any pending change ids?

noah: change batch shows status INSYNC but I suspect propagation caches still serving old record due to resolver caching. I'll bump the A record with a small TTL change trick.

noah: applying emergency change: set TTL to 30 for api.redwood.example.com then back to 300 after stabilization. Commands:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --change-batch file://change-ttl.json
```
(change-ttl.json contains the same A but TTL 30)

cloudflare-bot: Cloudflare API: purged cache for api.redwood.example.com (zone: ZCF123). Cloudflare edge caches cleared.

selina: rolling the change now. Notifying support about customer impact and status page update.

support-ops: FYI - two enterprise customers reported errors and were routed to support. Logged tickets.

jamie: after TTL change, probing again:
```
dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com A
# => 3.123.45.67
```
Looks like majority now resolving to healthy IPs. Errors trending down but still some resolvers with stale caches.

maria: taking 1hr oncall handoff at 20:00 UTC. If still flapping, escalate to cloud provider support. I'll keep monitoring.

noah: opened RDNS ticket with Route53, request expedited cache invalidation on their side — referencing change-id C123456789. Also cross-checked healthchecker - fine.

selina: TL;DR: cause = geo-dns propagation + some resolver cache divergence across providers causing traffic to hit decommissioned host. Mitigation = reduce TTL + route53 change + cloudflare cache purge + update Incident page + support outreach.

jamie: action items for postmortem: add forced publish step to runbook, include TTL ramp strategy before planned IP move, improve synthetic checks across multiple public resolvers, and add automated failover weight shift in Geodns during health anomalies.

selina: marking incident as 'mitigated' but not resolved. Will create postmortem and schedule follow-up with Product and NetEng tomorrow. :thumbsup:

cloudflare-bot: Reminder: Cloudflare support case CF-98765 opened (priority P2). Route53 case AWS-43210 acknowledged.

selina: thanks everyone. Handoff to maria for night watch. Maria please escalate if errors exceed 5% again.

maria: on it. monitoring dashboards up. ping me in #incidents if anything else.
